messages:
maya: Heads-up: a new customer hit a confusing flow in onboarding. SDK surfaced '400: bad request' but backend body had "error": "invalid_credentials" and message 'refresh_token expired'. No hint to reauth.
dan: That's a parity bug. Some SDKs parse body.error, others only use status codes. We should prefer explicit body codes when present.
rory: Proposal: mapping precedence should be body.code -> structured mapping table -> status code heuristics. The mapping table includes fields: code, friendly_message, action_hint (e.g., reauth, prompt-user, retry), retryable boolean.
maya: If SDKs return typed exceptions, include these fields on the exception object. For languages without typed exceptions return an error object with the same fields.
dan: Also add guidance for combined failures: expired token + auth service 502 during refresh. In that scenario, prefer action_hint=reauth instead of retrying, because reauth will surface the real issue to the user.
infra-bot: [ci] go-sdk tests failing: error_map_test.go: expected RefreshTokenError but got GenericBadRequest. https://ci.redwood.internal/9999
rory: I'll own the cross-SDK mapping spec and sample-app tests. Sample-apps should include fixtures for: expired refresh -> show reauth UI; expired refresh + auth 502 -> show reauth; 503 Retry-After -> exponential backoff.
maya: UX request: standardize user-facing copy in a central file so onboarding guides can render friendly messages instead of raw backend strings. Example: invalid_credentials -> "Your session has expired. Please sign in to continue." and action_hint: reauth.
dan: Implementation note for runtime: put a small response middleware that, when Content-Type is JSON, parses body for error/code fields and emits mapped error. Keep raw_body available for logs but not shown in UX.
rory: I'll add tests to sample-apps and a spec doc in devex docs. Owners: rory (spec + tests), dan (go-sdk fix), maya (onboarding copy). Target: next sprint.
